Memory.value: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
The world is a dangerous place
I was betrayed by someone I trusted

issues.item: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: The contamination appraisal is hard to reconcile with the trauma type of police violence in this profile. It is much more characteristic of sexual trauma or interpersonal violation with a strong disgust/shame component, and here there are no supporting memory, trigger, threat, or strategy items that would make this appraisal clinically coherent. The remaining items describe intrusive, alien, uncontrolled traumatic memory and general danger/body-reactivity beliefs, which fit severe PTSD, but the contamination item stands out as a trauma-incongruent appraisal.

vignette: Samantha, a 28-year-old European-American police officer in a relationship, has been struggling with intrusive memories and negative appraisals following a traumatic incident involving violence during her duty. The event left deep emotional scars that have begun to affect various aspects of her life. The incident occurred one night while Samantha was responding to an emergency call. As she approached the scene, she found herself caught in the crossfire between two officers who had turned on each other. Despite her attempts to intervene and de-escalate the situation, she was pushed into a dangerous confrontation that left her shaken and physically injured. Since then, Samantha has been plagued by full sensory reliving of the memory. When it comes back to her, she is transported back to that night, experiencing every detail vividly through all her senses. The memory feels alien, as if it belongs to someone else rather than herself, making it even more disturbing and unsettling. She often finds these memories forcing their way into her mind at unexpected moments, disrupting her daily activities and leading to intense distress. The recurring intrusive memories have also fueled Samantha's negative appraisals. She believes that her body is her enemy; it keeps reacting as if she is still in danger, even when she is safe. This heightened state of arousal has made her feel constantly on edge, making it difficult for her to relax or trust her surroundings. The memory of the betrayal by someone she trusted-a fellow officer-has deepened her perception that the world is a dangerous place. Her fear and mistrust have seeped into her work environment, affecting how she interacts with colleagues and approaching situations on duty. She has become hyper-vigilant and suspicious, often second-guessing her own judgment and questioning the intentions of those around her. This increased vigilance is not just a fleeting thought but a pervasive feeling that colors every interaction. One particular incident at work highlighted this cycle. During a routine patrol, Samantha heard a gunshot from nearby and immediately assumed the worst, her body responding instinctively as if she were back in that dangerous confrontation. The memory forced its way into her mind, overwhelming her with fear and confusion. This response led to an increase in her negative appraisals; she was certain that the world remained a dangerous place, reinforcing her belief that her body's reactions were justified. The constant cycle of intrusive memories and negative beliefs has taken a toll on Samantha's personal life as well. She finds herself withdrawing from social activities and avoiding situations where she might feel vulnerable or exposed. Even conversations with her partner about the incident are fraught; she feels like an outsider to her own experience, further isolating herself. What finally brought Samantha to seek help was a growing sense of hopelessness and fear that these symptoms would only worsen if left unaddressed. She is most afraid of becoming a shell of who she once was, unable to function effectively as both a police officer and in her relationship. Despite the challenges, she hopes for a way to break free from this cycle, to regain control over her thoughts and feelings, and ultimately feel safe again. Samantha's journey toward healing is driven by a desire to reclaim her sense of self and trust in the world around her, despite the lingering shadows of the traumatic event.
